sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Positive multinomial cells, randomized-instrument support, and target-mass positivity remain distinct conditions. Causal tangent legality additionally requires \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\) and \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\); both are certified from rational response-type face data.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On every fixed compact, base convergence and the centered local expansion imply eventual positive cells and lawful causal parameters. Carter then contributes only the bounded-ratio experiment error; the score mean, covariance, active-face remainder, rational offset, and semantic-union displacement are charged separately. The diagonal radius records exactly where all such compact moduli have passed, and no premise constrains a label boundary inserted beyond that radius.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: The unconditional contribution consists of three proved pieces: common-ray Foelner operators are path-independent and have explicit translation boundary ratios; Carter's bounded-ratio kernels yield fixed-compact and moving-offset multinomial transfer after separate semantic and covariance charges; and compact exhaustion yields a global lower limit together with two-sided convergence on computable expanding windows, but no global upper limit. Effective compatible density is now an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination remains conditional on an affirmative answer or a separately proved sufficient gluing package.

project_justification.gap: Carter's bounded-ratio comparison controls a fixed positive-cell multinomial experiment and its matched Gaussian experiment, but it does not compare moving causal truth regions or control parameters escaping every compact. At recession, common-ray commutativity does not control the Gaussian-weighted difference between incident face and cone rules on simultaneous collars. The remaining open question is whether the encoded rational geometry admits computable canonical-section safety, positive-weight candidate safety, translated-uniform tails, and a refinement schedule with total error tending to zero.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification inference combines discontinuous completed labels, intersecting unbounded recession faces, and a global honesty constraint. Exact agreement on a geometric face does not control all candidates mixed nearby, while compact local asymptotics cannot detect a hard seam escaping to infinity. The proved compact/windowed transfer and the unresolved noncompact gluing problem are therefore mathematically distinct.
project_justification.fill: The paper solves common-ray operator coherence, Carter-based fixed-compact and moving-offset transfer with separate semantic and covariance error terms, a global minimax lower limit, and two-sided convergence on computable expanding windows. It does not prove global effective compatible density. That construction is posed explicitly as an open-ended question, and CertGluePFL termination is claimed only under an affirmative ECD result or a separately proved sufficient gluing package.

body.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) supplies only the bounded-ratio comparison between fixed positive-cell multinomial experiments and their matched multivariate normal experiments through parameter-independent kernels. The present work separately handles score maps, covariance replacement, completed-affine-arrangement stability, moving offsets, and expanding lawful windows. Blanco, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2013) provide the Job Corps wage-effect partial-identification setting; that causal application does not supply recession gluing. Day and Markov--Kakutani invariant-mean theory and Namioka's 1964 Foelner conditions concern a single amenable commuting action and provide neither an input-computable modulus nor semantic coverage, separated-risk safety, translated-tail control, or branching-refinement complexity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Effective compatible density is unresolved under the standing assumptions. The missing construction must preserve every active \(D_v\), \(H_r\), and protected star on canonical sections; certify every candidate with positive collar weight; prove exact overlap traces or an honest Gaussian-weighted face--cone discrepancy bound on simultaneous supports; control guard and normal-base tails uniformly over translated means; and compute refinement counts \(N_j\) and schedules \(L_j,B_j,\delta_j\) for which all accumulated errors vanish and \(N_j/L_j\to0\). No refinement-independent ledger constant is assumed. Consequently the milliscale four-label certificate and unconditional global CertGluePFL termination also remain unresolved.
body.honest_scope: The causal target is the same-law joint identified set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp endpoint intervals; no Cartesian joint sharpness is claimed. Carter-backed sampled-data results are fixed-compact or expanding-window statements. Compact exhaustion proves the global lower limit and two-sided windowed convergence, but neither a global \(\limsup\) nor a globally honest unbounded sampled-data primal. Common-ray coherence, Gaussian smoothing, one-chart averaging, and fixed-library weighted telescoping are proved. Global effective compatible density is an open-ended question, so CertGluePFL termination and replayable global Gaussian certification are conditional rather than established.
body.interpretation: The Gaussian experiment is the valid local decision target on every fixed lawful direction window. Its minimax value is the limit of the expanding-window multinomial values and a lower limit for the original global values; the compact-uniform premises imply no global upper limit. The common-ray library is an algebraically coherent recession representation, not a compatibility-density theorem. The missing step is simultaneous safe gluing across actual collar supports with a computable growing-refinement ledger.
